name: Second-floor en suite

current.summary: New en-suite shower room off the bedroom, mostly built but not finished. Walk-in shower at the end: deep-blue glazed tiles laid vertically, large grey stone-effect tiles on the side, a tiled niche, black rain-shower head, a raised tiled shower floor with a square drain. No glass screen — a curtain on a tension rod for now. Close-coupled WC against a half-height band of the blue tiles. In the corner, a vanity made of two oak shelves with a round white countertop basin; the black tap is not yet fitted, a mirror is propped behind, and bare wires hang from the wall above for a light. Half-height blue tiling runs round the room with white walls above; a blue-tiled sill at the window, whose shutters are patched with filler. A high plastered ledge holds baskets, with an old beam exposed in the recess above. Recessed downlights and colour-changing LED lighting. Floor: light-grey tiles.
keep: Blue vertical tiles and grey tiles
issues: JOB 1 — Fit the basin properly: tap, waste and trap connected, basin fixed and sealed to the oak top
JOB 2 — Shower doors in place of the curtain
Proposed by Claude (not yet agreed): Wall light over the basin: connect the bare wires (make them safe meanwhile); hang the mirror
Proposed by Claude (not yet agreed): WC: the flexible supply hose loops out visibly — shorten or re-route
Proposed by Claude (not yet agreed): Tile edges: the top of the half-height tiling and the shower wall ends need a trim or a neat painted line and sealant
Proposed by Claude (not yet agreed): Window shutters and door: sand the filler and paint
Proposed by Claude (not yet agreed): Exposed beam: clean, treat, seal; tidy the plaster edge around it

target.concept: The room is designed — blue vertical tiles, grey stone-effect tiles, oak vanity, black fittings. Target is to finish it: a working, sealed basin and a proper glass shower enclosure.

palette.name: Matt black
palette.role: tap, shower fittings, shower door frame

furniture.name: Shower doors
furniture.detail: Recommendation: black-framed sliding door on a fixed panel, to match the top-floor bathroom and the black fittings here. Measure the opening width at the kerb and at head height (old walls are rarely parallel) and the height available. If the opening is under about 80 cm, a single pivot or bi-fold door instead.

surfaces.prep: Seal the oak first: 3 coats hardwax-oil or marine varnish on all faces, including the cut-outs for tap and waste. Drill the top for the tap and waste if not done.
surfaces.finish: Fit the black tap with flexible connectors to isolating valves; fit click-clack waste and a black or chrome bottle trap (it will be visible under the shelf); bed the basin on clear sanitary silicone; test for leaks
surfaces.notes: Keep the trap and pipes neat — they show between the two shelves

surfaces.prep: Remove the tension rod and curtain. Check the tiled kerb is level and falls inward to the drain
surfaces.finish: Fit enclosure to the tiled walls with the maker's wall profiles; silicone outside edges only; 6–8 mm safety glass
surfaces.notes: Drill tiles through the grout lines where possible; diamond bit, no hammer action

notes: Electrician to make safe / connect the wires above the basin before the mirror goes up
